commit.message:
cpuid: Preserve newer extended leaves

Clamping the AMD extended CPUID limit to 0x8000001f hides newer
KVM-supported leaves from guest feature discovery. Preserve KVM's
limit while retaining the existing minimum for topology leaves.

This lets Linux discover mitigation capabilities in leaf 0x80000021.
As documented upstream [0], SRSO_USER_KERNEL_NO tells Linux that Safe
RET is unnecessary at the user/kernel boundary.

On a Ryzen 9 9950X, the guest switches from retpolines and Safe RET
to eIBRS and VMEXIT-only SRSO mitigation. The stress-ng x86syscall
microbenchmark using getpid recorded median time per operation
falling from 86.59 to 28.86 ns (67%), with the same reduction in
guest CPU time per operation.

Keep this in the AMD transformer. Intel does not clamp this limit,
and AArch64 uses separate CPU feature discovery.

[0] https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/hw-vuln/srso.html#system-information-and-options
